AutomaticGuitarSimulator.interpret:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Parses a space-separated chord string stored in self.play_text into a list of dicts, each splitting one segment into its leading alphabetic chord name and its trailing non-alpha modifier, with optional per-segment display output." interpret]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> display </REF>: bool "When true, calls self.display for each parsed segment as a side effect; defaults to false and does not affect the returned list."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> play_list </REF>: list "List of dicts with keys 'Chord' (leading alphabetic prefix of the segment, may be empty string) and 'Tune' (remaining non-alpha suffix of the segment, may be empty string); empty list if self.play_text is blank or whitespace-only."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Strip self.play_text and check whether the result is empty or whitespace-only; if so, return an empty list immediately and skip all remaining steps. RESULT early_return_guard]
            [COMMAND Initialize play_list as an empty list to accumulate result dicts. RESULT play_list]
            [COMMAND Split self.play_text on a single space character to produce play_segs, a list of raw segment strings. RESULT play_segs]
            [COMMAND For each play_seg in play_segs: initialize pos to 0, then iterate over each character ele in play_seg left to right; if ele is alphabetic, increment pos by 1 and continue to the next character; on the first non-alphabetic character break out of the inner loop immediately; after the inner loop pos holds the count of leading alphabetic characters, or the full length of play_seg if every character was alphabetic. RESULT pos]
            [COMMAND Within the outer loop over play_segs, after the inner scan completes: assign play_chord as play_seg sliced from index 0 to pos (the alphabetic prefix), and assign play_value as play_seg sliced from pos to the end (the non-alpha remainder); both may be empty strings. RESULT play_chord, play_value]
            [COMMAND Within the outer loop over play_segs, append a dict with key 'Chord' set to play_chord and key 'Tune' set to play_value to play_list. RESULT play_list]
            [COMMAND Within the outer loop over play_segs, if display is truthy call self.display with play_chord and play_value as arguments; this fires once per segment and does not alter play_list. RESULT display_side_effect]
            [COMMAND After all segments are processed, return play_list. RESULT play_list]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: self.play_text is empty or contains only whitespace after stripping]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return an empty list immediately without executing any further logic. RESULT empty_list]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
AutomaticGuitarSimulator.display:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Formats a chord key and its associated tune value into a fixed human-readable string using Python's legacy percent-style string interpolation." display]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> key </REF>: any "The chord identifier; coerced to string via __str__ and inserted into the first placeholder of the format template"
        <REF> value </REF>: any "The tune value associated with the chord; coerced to string via __str__ and inserted into the second placeholder of the format template"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: string "A formatted string of the form 'Normal Guitar Playing -- Chord: <key>, Play Tune: <value>' with both inputs substituted in order"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Apply Python percent-style string formatting to the literal template 'Normal Guitar Playing -- Chord: %s, Play Tune: %s', substituting str(key) into the first %s slot and str(value) into the second %s slot RESULT formatted_string]
            [COMMAND Return formatted_string immediately to the caller without any further mutation or storage RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: Either key or value is None]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Coerce the None argument to the literal string 'None' via %s formatting; no exception is raised and the formatted string is returned normally RESULT formatted_string_with_none_literal]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: key or value is a non-string object with a custom or default __str__ implementation]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Coerce the object to its __str__ representation, which may be a default repr such as '<MyObj object at 0x...>' if no meaningful __str__ is defined; embed the result in the template and return RESULT formatted_string_with_repr]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
